newsitem.title: CANADA: Mexico transit consortium to get go-ahead-official.
newsitem.headline: Mexico transit consortium to get go-ahead-official.

text.p: A consortium that includes Bombardier Inc and Siemens AG is expected to get the go-ahead to build a C$600 million transit train system in the Mexican state of Guanajuato, an aide to the state governor told Reuters.

"A contract will be signed in October or November for the financing of the project. The contract will be given to Bombardier, Siemens, Arno and GMAT," Guanajuato assistant governor Fermin Salcedo Courtade told Reuters in an interview.
"We will start the work in early 1998 and finish by the year 2000," he said.
Courtade made his comments in Quebec City where he was discussing plans by Guanajuato Governor Vicente Fox Quesada to visit Quebec in October.
The consortium includes GMAT Ltd, a Montreal-based transportation company, and Arno Electrique Ltee, of Trois-Rivieres, Quebec, which specializes in the installation of electrical equipment.
Bombardier Transportation Group spokeswoman Francine Durocher-Monin said market studies had not been completed on the project.
"We have to finish our market studies and financing has to be arranged to assure the project's viability," she said.
Monin could not say whether the consortium's plans include the building of a new rail infrastructure for the project. Original plans were that construction would begin earlier this year.
"The investors waited because of the country's political and economic instability," said GMAT spokesman Normand Nadeau.

Heavily industrialized Guanajauato has a population of 4.5 million, and is 500 km north of Mexico City. General Motors, France's Groupe Danone and Mexico's state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) have major plants in the region.
The proposed 170-km-long transit system will link 11 cities in the state, including Leon, Guanajuato, Irapuato, Salamanca, Silao and Celaya.
